newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK GOVT PARTNER SEEKS RENEWAL OF DEATH PENALTY.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK GOVT PARTNER SEEKS RENEWAL OF DEATH PENALTY.

text.p: The ultra-right Slovak National Party (SNS), a junior member of the country's ruling government coalition, on Friday said it would initiate a referendum on reinstating the death penalty.

"We will initiate a referendum on the re-introduction of capital punishment in Slovakia at next week's parliamentary sesison," SNS chairman Jan Slota was quoted by the official news agency TASR as saying.
TASR said Slota was confident that the question of capital punishment would also again come up for discussion in the European Union (EU).
"There are signals from the EU that some of its members are also considering reviving the death penalty," Slota said.
An SNS party official who refused to be named told Reuters "the SNS still considers the the re-introduction of capital punishment as one of the pillars of its political programme."
Last year the government of Vladimir Meciar, of the main coalition partner the HZDS asked the Council of Europe (CE) to state its views on Slovakia's considerations to revive the death penalty.
The Council refused even considering Slovakia's proposal on the grounds that the death penalty violated basic human rights and freedoms.
Slovakia abolished capital punishment in 1990, but Meciar's HZDS and the SNS, made it one of the top priorities of their political platforms in the 1994 election campaign.
